build: Fresh standalone pinned swift-argument-parser clone; fresh scratch; ArgumentParser target with ArgumentParserToolInfo; --enable-index-store; discover and require one actual completed index; source compilation measured separately.
correctness: Exact source-ID sets and minimum depths at 1/3/5, explicit negatives, and all 13 audited incoming call edges before the depth-5 frontier. Extra/ambiguous/unmapped reachable identities fail. Oracle expectations are never filtered using tool output.
discovery: Measured separately: actual index-dump unit/record subprocesses plus generic source normalization and graph assembly; native Cartograph graph plus its own source normalization. Native outputs and graph caches persist.
first: First observed query workflow follows separately measured discovery in both arms; no cold-cache claim. First discovery plus first query is separately reported, without summing RSS.
identity: Each arm independently binds all source-declared callable locations. Expected source selectors require unique USRs; all other in-scope callers remain eligible false positives. No bare-name or type-owner aliasing.
interpretation: Depths are correlated boundary checks from one immutable source state. Descriptive validation timings cannot establish final edit-refresh session cost, independent cold samples, universal superiority, or the final holdout decision gate. No superiority conclusion is emitted.
native_depth_contract: Separate depth 1/3/5 native commands check CLI boundaries and exact answers. Their measured costs are retained separately, outside repeated combined-user-task timings.
queries: Same combined reverse-caller user task: one depth-5 minimum-distance answer also supplies depth-1/3 subsets. Baseline reuses its persisted actual-CLI call graph and runs one external BFS in a new Python process. Cartograph executes one native query --batch --depth 5 in a new CLI process. No repeated dumps of unchanged records are imposed on the baseline. Native Cartograph ingestion remains part of its CLI query cost.
repeated: Even preregistered repetition count with shuffled balanced AB/BA order plus separately labelled first workload; one diagnostic arm on Linux. New processes, likely warm uncontrolled OS caches; no persistent MCP sessions. All runs retained; errors/timeouts fail and retain raw evidence.
role: real-project validation only; not the final holdout
rss: wait4 ru_maxrss normalized to bytes; outer worker value is the OS-reported high-water statistic, not simultaneous aggregate process-tree RSS. Native child values retained separately. Do not sum peak RSS or infer token cost from raw bytes.
shared_input: Identical physical completed store, source hashes, compiler version/target, binary hashes, and selected libIndexStore bytes. Index/source fingerprints checked after discovery and every workload.
source_oracle: Frozen source-only audit; neither arm supplies or changes expected answers. Unknown compiler representations fail for human review.
state_regimes: Persisted generic baseline graph versus fresh native Cartograph CLI ingestion are different state regimes. Descriptive timings are not a fair final persistent-session performance comparison. Final 10-query sessions must offer equivalent reuse to each arm, including available native/MCP session reuse.
timing: Parent workflow clock includes request writes, worker startup, cache reads, subprocesses, JSON parsing, normalization, answer serialization, and evidence writes. Outer wait4 wall/RSS additionally recorded for every worker; each native invocation has separate wait4 wall/RSS. Common compilation and correctness grading excluded from query clocks.
